title: Power Pages: environment-level governance of external authentication providers
summary: The briefing passes: the authentication default, enforcement behaviour and governance routes are supported, and the cited Learn pages opened successfully despite the earlier rate limits. Minor corrections should complete the routes to their policy choices, use the full targeting labels, acknowledge published product-level licensing and note the release plan's different availability date.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment / Change & support; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Enforcing authentication restrictions can affect sign-in on live sites.
claims.quote: These controls can change how users sign in to live sites. Before you restrict an authentication option, align with the owners of the affected sites and plan the change together. Their users might not have another way to sign in.

claims.claim: A governance restriction takes precedence over an existing maker configuration.
claims.quote: If an existing site configuration uses a sign-in method associated with a blocked option, the governance setting takes precedence.

claims.where: Governance controls prose; Risk assessment / Change & support; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Users of existing sites can no longer authenticate through an option once governance blocks it.
claims.quote: When a governance setting that blocks an authentication option takes effect, users can no longer sign in or register by using that authentication option.

claims.claim: The authentication governance Learn page does not specify the exact administrator role required.
claims.quote: Searched: roles in the full external-auth-control page and admin-center-security. The authentication page addresses admins without naming a required role; the security dashboard page's roles govern viewing that dashboard, not configuring authentication governance.

claims.claim: Tenant administrators configure non-production public-access governance.
claims.quote: Tenant admins can control whether makers can make a Power Pages site public when either the site or its environment is non-production.

claims.fix: Feature-specific licensing remains unpublished, but unknown understates published product licensing. Set licensing.model to 'included' and licensing.notes to 'An option within Power Pages, whose licensing is capacity based for authenticated users per website/month and anonymous users per website/month, through subscriptions or pay-as-you-go meters.
